text.p: Here are the highligts of the stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for thier accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Serbia and Montenegro will never be servants to anyone, said Zoran Lilic, the Socialist Party of Serbia (SPS) presidental candidate, at the Montenegro's ruling Democratic Party of Socialists (DPS) congress in Kolasin.
- State must upgrade mining production through investments, said Dragan Tomic, Serbian parliament speaker and acting republic's president.
- Prices of meat reduced under government pressure.
- Cattle breeders and slaughter houses are against imports and meat price increase, Serbian Chamber of Commerce said.
- Transport system from Veliki Krivelj copper mine to Bor will be completed by the end of the year and will reduce copper production costs by 30 percent.
- Foreign investors interested in Serbia's power company Elektroprivreda Srbije (EPS), said EPS's executive director Slobodan Babic.
- In January-June period 153 registered murders and 152 attempted murders in Serbia.
NASA BORBA
- Dissident faction of DPS proposed Momir Bulatovic for presidental candidate.

- Kragujevac arms factory workers on marching strike since Tuesday expected to arrive to Belgrade on Thursday. Police prevented some 100 walking protestors to use highway and banned their gathering in front of the Serbian government. Workers accuse Yugoslav President Slobodan Milosevic for their difficult position.
- Foreign investors in Yugoslavia discouraged by huge foreign trade deficit, enormous labour surplus and book-keeping disorder.
- Slovenia's lawyers considering appeal on the Cyprus court decision to reject Slovenia's claim from Beogradska Banka Cyprus.
- Belgian Interbrew unpleasantly surprised by Niksic Brewery management demands.
- Beobanka starts opening savings accounts in association with Greek partner on Thursday.
- The Fund for Humanitarian Law says thousands of people in Serbia and Montenegro in panic because of fear from the Hague war crimes tribunal.
- Will French MTC Peugeot and Yugoslav Verano Motors make a deal on assembling scooters in Yugoslavia?
- Serbia will invest 345 million dinars to modernise its asbestos mine Rudnik azbesta Korlace and increase its annual production to 6,400 tonnes from current 2,000 tonnes.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Participation of grey economy in GDP will be halved through extensive federal government measures; cash in circulation to be reduced and non-cash payments stimulated, said Yugoslav Internal Trade Minister Milorad Miskovic.
-- M O N T E N E G R O --
POBJEDA
- There are between 130,000-140,000 tourists in Montenegro at present, said Montenegrin Minister for Tourism Ivo Armenko.

- Momir Bulatovic elected DPS president at the congress of dissident faction of the party. Milo Djukanovic, Svetozar Marovic and Milica-Pejanovic Djurisic releaved of their duties as DPS's deputy presidents. -- Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 311 4305
